# M0-S5 I4: a Go-syntax package inside a loGo/s module is still governed
# by the module's cgo policy. The module uses cgo="restricted" with an
# empty allowlist. The check keys on the main module's kind, not on the
# package's own file kinds, so ./gp fails with the allowlist error. It is
# not mixed_module: that diagnostic needs both kinds loaded, and building
# ./gp alone loads only the Go package. ok/ is a pure loGo/s package that
# is never built; it exists so the module classifies as loGo/s instead of
# Go, which is what engages the policy.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# Default CC: a host compiler setting must not drive the build.
env CC=

# Clear any host CGO_ENABLED so the restricted key alone decides.
env CGO_ENABLED=

# With an empty allowlist every cgo package is refused, including the
# Go-syntax one. The -o flag keeps the RED-run binary off directory gp.
[cgo] ! logos build -o gp.bin ./gp
[cgo] stderr '\[restriction::cgo_usage\] package example\.com/m/gp uses cgo and is not in cgo_allowlist'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/m

go 1.27

-- logos.toml --
[build]
cgo = "restricted"
cgo_allowlist = []

-- ok/ok.lgo --
package ok

// Answer reports a constant.
func Answer() int {
	return 42
}

-- gp/main.go --
package main

/*
int answer() { return 42; }
*/
import "C"

import "fmt"

func main() { fmt.Println("gp:", C.answer()) }
